CBSA.CICSBSA.ABNDFILE.recovery_why: etc/install/base/installjcl/BANK.csd: DEFINE FILE(ABNDFILE) ... RECOVERY(NONE) -- the abend log a backout must not undo

notes: CBSA's inquire-customer service (INQCUST, LINKed by BNK1DCS -- transaction ODCS -- and by INQACCCU and CREACC with the INQCUST copybook's COMMAREA). It sets 'N' / '0', keys on the program's own sort code (SORTCODE copybook, 987654; INQCUST-SCODE is ignored) and INQCUST-CUSTNO. INQCUST-CUSTNO 9999999999 or 0000000000 first finds the last customer number with a backwards browse (STARTBR at HIGH-VALUES, READPREV, ENDBR; any failure 'N' / '9' and RETURN): the number of the file's highest key, whatever its sort code. 9999999999 then reads that number; 0000000000 reads a random one, (last - 1) * FUNCTION RANDOM(EIBTASKN) + 1, drawing again (FUNCTION RANDOM with no seed) on each NOTFND up to 1,000 times. READ NORMAL fills the COMMAREA from the record, 'Y'; NOTFND gives 'N' / '1' (blanking name and address on an ordinary number; 9999999999 looks the last customer up once more); any other condition fills ABNDINFO, LINKs ABNDPROC (run in the same task: an ABNDFILE record) and ABENDs CVR1 CANCEL. Each SYSIDERR on a file command is retried after a DELAY FOR SECONDS(3), up to 100 times. FUNCTION RANDOM runs on the oracle's generator (oracle_assumptions.md C12) seeded by EIBTASKN, a stated fact of the run (X21): the random customers are the oracle's, not z/OS's. Not reached: ABEND-HANDLING (the HANDLE ABEND exit runs for an abend AFCR / AFCS / AFCT from VSAM RLS, which no fault raises; the program's own ABEND CVR1 is CANCEL) and the 100-retry ends of the SYSIDERR loops. Data: customer.txt is SYNTHETIC (CBSA generates its customers at random with BANKDATA; the corpus ships none): customers 1-5 and 8 of sort code 987654, one of 123456 and a decoy 999999/0000000003 holding the highest key; abndfile.bin is empty. CUSTOMER and ABNDFILE are compared after every scenario. Derived from the CICS Bank Sample Application (CBSA, github.com/cicsdev/cics-banking-sample-application-cbsa; Copyright IBM Corp. 2023), licensed under the Eclipse Public License 2.0: LICENSE here is the corpus's own; NOTICE says what is derived.

scenarios.name: found
scenarios.why: READ 987654/0000000001 NORMAL: every field of the record into the COMMAREA, 'Y' / '0'

scenarios.name: found-boundary-values
scenarios.why: credit score 000, born 01/01/1900, a 22-character name and a 34-character address padded to 60 / 160

scenarios.name: found-leap-day
scenarios.why: born and reviewed on 29 February; credit score 999

scenarios.name: found-after-gap
scenarios.why: the customer after the gap (6 and 7 do not exist)

scenarios.name: not-found
scenarios.why: READ NOTFND on an ordinary number: 'N' / '1', INQCUST-NAME and INQCUST-ADDR blanked; the rest of the COMMAREA (eyecatcher, number, credit score) left as the caller sent it

scenarios.name: other-sortcode-ignored
scenarios.why: INQCUST-SCODE 123456 is not the key: the program reads its own sort code 987654, so customer 987654/1 comes back and INQCUST-SCODE is overwritten with 987654

scenarios.name: only-other-sortcode
scenarios.why: 987654/3 exists as well as the decoy 999999/3: the program's own sort code wins

scenarios.name: last-customer
scenarios.why: 9999999999: GET-LAST-CUSTOMER-VSAM -- STARTBR at HIGH-VALUES, READPREV gives the file's highest key 999999/0000000003 (another sort code: the program keeps only its number), ENDBR, 'Y'; then READ 987654/0000000003 NORMAL: customer 987654/3 returned

scenarios.name: random-customer
scenarios.why: 0000000000: the last customer number (3) as above, then RANDOM-CUSTOMER = (3 - 1) * FUNCTION RANDOM(EIBTASKN) + 1 truncated to 1 or 2 (EIBTASKN 0, oracle_assumptions.md X21; the generator, C12), READ NORMAL

scenarios.name: random-customer-task-12345
scenarios.why: the same with EIBTASKN 12345 as RANDOM's seed

scenarios.name: random-customer-retry

faults.why: 13 on the first READ: GENERATE-RANDOM-CUSTOMER-AGAIN (the next FUNCTION RANDOM), the second READ NORMAL

scenarios.why: random customer not found once: INQCUST-RETRY 1, a second random number, found

scenarios.name: random-customer-gives-up
scenarios.why: every random customer not found: after INQCUST-RETRY reaches 1000 the loop ends with 'N' / '1' (the name and address left as they were)

scenarios.name: last-customer-notfound-retried

faults.why: 13 on the first READ: GET-LAST-CUSTOMER-VSAM again, WS-V-RETRIED 'Y'

scenarios.why: 9999999999 and the READ NOTFND once: the last customer is looked up again (a second browse) and the second READ finds 987654/3

scenarios.name: last-customer-notfound-twice
scenarios.why: 9999999999 and NOTFND on the retry too: no IF of RCV010 takes it (the retried flag is set and the number is 9999999999), so the catch-all abends: ABNDINFO filled, LINK ABNDPROC (an ABNDFILE record), ABEND CVR1 CANCEL

scenarios.name: read-io-error
scenarios.why: READ IOERR: ABNDINFO filled from the clock and EIB (APPLID CBSAREGN, RESP 17), LINK ABNDPROC writes it to ABNDFILE, ABEND CVR1 CANCEL (no HANDLE ABEND exit)

scenarios.name: read-sysiderr-retried

faults.why: 53 on the first READ: DELAY 3 seconds, READ again

scenarios.why: SYSIDERR once: the retry loop DELAYs (a task takes no time, X4) and READs again, NORMAL: 'Y'

scenarios.name: read-sysiderr-then-notfound

faults.why: 53 on the first READ; the retry's READ NOTFND naturally

scenarios.why: SYSIDERR then NOTFND: the loop ends on a condition other than SYSIDERR, and RCV010's NOTFND IF gives 'N' / '1'

scenarios.name: startbr-fails
scenarios.why: STARTBR IOERR: 'N' / '9', and P010 RETURNs at once without a READ

scenarios.name: startbr-notfound-random
scenarios.why: the random path's browse fails the same way: 'N' / '9', RETURN

scenarios.name: startbr-sysiderr-retried
scenarios.why: SYSIDERR on STARTBR once: DELAY, STARTBR again NORMAL, the browse goes on: 'Y', customer 987654/3

scenarios.name: readprev-fails
scenarios.why: READPREV IOERR: 'N' / '9', RETURN (the browse is left open; the task ends it)

scenarios.name: readprev-sysiderr-retried
scenarios.why: SYSIDERR on READPREV once: DELAY, READPREV again, the last record read

scenarios.name: endbr-fails-ignored
scenarios.why: ENDBR IOERR: the program tests ENDBR's RESP only inside its SYSIDERR IF (the END-IF is missing, so the test sits under that IF), so the failure is ignored: 'Y' and the READ goes on

scenarios.name: endbr-sysiderr-then-fails
scenarios.why: SYSIDERR on ENDBR, then IOERR on the retry: the loop ends, the RESP test inside the IF gives 'N' / '9', RETURN

scenarios.name: endbr-sysiderr-retried
scenarios.why: SYSIDERR on ENDBR once, then NORMAL: 'Y'
